# Shared-ToDo Pilot Plugin

`shared-todo` (`berg-plugin-shared-todo`) is the real, end-to-end pilot
plugin: it installs and runs without touching `berg-agents` source.
It
exists to validate discovery, config, tools, generic tool dispatch, UI
mounting, and cross-tab synchronization before any other plugin follows
the pattern.
If a plugin works end to end as `shared-todo` does, it is
conformant.

## Identity

  | Key           | Value                                          |
  | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
  | Package Path  | `berg_plugins/shared-todo/`                    |
  | Plugin ID     | `berg-plugin-shared-todo`                      |
  | Manifest      | `berg_plugins/shared-todo/plugin.yaml`         |
  | Entry         | `shared_todo.shared_todo:SharedToDoPlugin`     |
  | Python dist   | `pyproject.toml` -> `berg-plugins` entry point |
  | Frontend dist | `ui/dist/todo-surface.js` (built, not source)  |

## Manifest `ui:` block

Shared-ToDo was the first plugin to own its own UI.
See
`docs/plugins/PLUGIN-UI.qmd` for the full contract.
Its manifest
declares:

```yaml
ui:
  entry:  \"ui/dist/todo-surface.js\"
  export: \"TodoSurface\"
  placement: \"side-panel\"
  label: \"📋 Todos\"
  width: 340
```

## Tools (10)

Tools are ordinary Python functions exposed to the model as agent-facing
tools, plus a `list_todo_items` helper registered as a UI capability.
All communication between the plugin UI and the backend now goes only
through the generic dispatch path.

### Todos

- `create_todo(title, description?, subtasks?)`
- `list_todos()` --- model-ready Markdown summary
- `list_todo_items()` --- structured snapshot used by the UI
- `update_todo(id, title, description?, status?)`
- `complete_todo(id)`
- `delete_todo(id)`

### Subtasks

Subtasks are stored inside each todo's Markdown as a `## Subtasks`
checklist (`- [ ]` / `- [x]`) so hand edits stay safe.

- `add_subtask(todo_id, text)`
- `set_subtask_done(todo_id, subtask_index, done)`
- `rename_subtask(todo_id, subtask_index, text)`
- `delete_subtask(todo_id, subtask_index)`

`update_todo` preserves existing subtasks and any notes across rewrites;
the separate toggle tools do not.

## Generic dispatch

The host exposes one call shape:

`POST /api/plugins/{plugin_id}/tools/{tool}` --- backend:

1. validates plugin exists and is enabled,
2. resolves the actual tool (by plug-in tool name *or* function
   `__name__`, so non-model-facing helpers remain callable),
3. runs it with the project as the working directory,
4. returns non-string results as JSON.

The shared-todo UI uses only `apiFetch` against that endpoint.
Nothing
todo-specific remains in `berg_agents/ui/routes.py` or `schemas.py`.

## Config

Shared-ToDo config is read from `.berg-agents/.shared_todo/config.yaml`
(single config resolver --- see `CONFIGURATION.qmd`).
The plugin also
records a separate `sharedtodos/` user-data directory (three existing
Markdown todos in this repo).
Those files and their contents are user
data; never delete or overwrite them as part of an installation/update.

If your config is empty/invalid, the plugin degrades to its schema
defaults; discovery and capability registration still succeed.

## Capabilities registration

Plugin tools are registered as `ToolCapability` entries and discovered by
`PluginManager` inside each chat turn, plus `list_chat_plugins` for the
UI/status badges.
Turning the plugin OFF (through the Plugins panel)
removes its tools from the next turn.
New todo items created or updated
by the plugin surface are visible to the agent on the next turn without
a restart; the sidebar surface refreshes on `refreshKey` bumps.

## UI notes

- UI runs as a built bundle; the host mounts it with one React instance.
- Side panel defaults to `width: 340`, but a drag divider lets the user
  resize it (280px -- viewport minus 420px).
  Manifest `width` is now a
  historical hint, not a hard lock.
- Subtask toggles must be plain accessible buttons in this HeroUI
  version --- `Checkbox`/`CheckboxField` does not move inside a
  `CheckboxGroup`; the pilot verified toggling both directions.
- Cache `no-cache` applies to ` /berg-plugins/*`, so rebuilds appear on
  the next navigation without a hard reload.

## Install / change / verify

1. `cd berg_plugins/shared-todo && bun run build:ui`
2. Confirm output lands at `ui/dist/todo-surface.js` (git-ignored?
   **Not** ignored --- the built file is tracked as the shippable artifact).
3. Start / restart the server.
4. `GET /api/plugins` --- expect `berg-plugin-shared-todo`, 10 tools,
   `ui.entry_built: true`.
5. In the web UI, click **📋 Todos** --- side panel renders; toggle
   survives both directions.

Quick backend verification (non-interactive, cheap):

```sh
python -m berg_agents.plugin_system.chat_integration list  # prints plugins + capabilities
```
